utterances.text: Now, did you tell the Defence that you may have heard something about this, whereas then I would expect the statement to be: I heard that this and this was the case in Omarska, instead of: This happened in Omarska, because you don't know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did hear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I'm telling you this because if you want this Chamber to take your evidence seriously, then please be accurate and do not tell us all kind of things you later say you don't know, because that may affect the credibility of your testimony, and I'm telling you this because you have been called by the Defence in order to function here as a witness. You could spoil it, you could spoil your own evidence if you're not accurate and precise. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Mandic, let's talk about something that I believe you will and should know, and that's the following. Were you aware that massive crimes had been committed against the Muslims in the Prijedor region and particularly against the people who were held in those camps?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO MANDIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly how to answer. I heard there was torture against non-Serbs in Omarska and in Trnopolje as well, there were killings, but I didn't see any of it myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let me ask you about a very specific -- go ahead, sir.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO MANDIC
utterances.text: I don't know if this is satisfactory as an answer to you. I don't know how else to express myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you about a specific period and about some specific crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if I could begin by calling up 65 ter 11302, please. And if we could turn to page 5 of this document in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, the overall document is an UNPROFOR document reflecting information sent to members of the European community, and a portion of it is a letter from Mr. Izetbegovic on July 26th, 1992, which reflects the following at the top of page 5: "In the meantime," and it -- and the "meantime" as shown by the earlier portion of the letter refers to since the London talks. "In the meantime, new mass crimes have been committed against the civilian population, particularly in the Prijedor region." And goes on to say: "And now concentration camps have been set up in various parts of Bosnia and Herzegovina." Now, do you have a -- first of all, just to set the timing of this, do you recall, sir, on your own - and I could show you a document if you don't - that the London talks ceased for a period on about July 17th and then were anticipated to resume later in the month?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Maybe if you told him the year too.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It's all 1992. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, let me just quickly to set this call 65 ter 10729. I need to inform Mr. Lukic that this is a document that I -- one document I think that didn't make it to our notification list, and I apologise for that, but it's being used for a very limited contextual purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What I'm showing you, sir, and I'll have to read it to you in English, is an article by Craig Whitney to the New York Times, and the reason I bring it to your attention is the date line is London, July 17, 1992. It refers --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, is there any dispute about this part or is it important that the witness remembers himself?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, no. Not at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there's any dispute, Mr. Lukic, about London talks stopped 17th July and to be resumed later that month?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't know if that's the intention of my learned friend to ask me or the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I was asking you --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Of course not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- whether there's any dispute about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Of course not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So I wanted to focus on that period of time, so specifically - and that is, I'd ask you about massive crimes against non-Serbs particularly in those facilities - now I was focusing on the period between roughly July 20th and July 26th or July 17th and July 26th. So let me ask you: Were you aware of the massacre in Room 3 at Keraterm on the night of 24th through 25th of July, 1992, about which this Court has received evidence?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO MANDIC
utterances.text: That was a killing that took place one night, a killing of several residents. I believe I remember. I think it was Zigic who did it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It's a massacre of in excess of 100 people.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO MANDIC
utterances.text: Yes, massacre. I agree, it was a massacre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now your reference to Zigic, is this what you heard or did he kill them --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Heard, I heard about it. I didn't have any experience myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have no personal knowledge and you heard that Zigic killed during the night 100 persons just on his own, is that what you heard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Whether he was alone or several people were involved, I can't remember the details now. I know that this happened and I believe it was Zigic, but I don't know if anybody was with him. I believe this case was tried and the court was aware of all the details. I can't remember now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you were aware that that happened to persons detained in Keraterm camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you aware of the cleansing operations that took place in the Brdo, Biscani, Ljubija, and Brezevo areas during that same period of time; that is, in the latter part of July 1992? During which the army and the police swept through those areas, rounding up many, many, many people and during which hundreds of non-Serbs were killed.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO MANDIC
utterances.text: I know that there was mopping-up, looking for the remaining extremists. One of them even came to see me at my home, his name was Zec. A local police officer brought him to me. We knew each other from school --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, Witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- and I said: I'm sorry, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, please respond to what Mr. Tieger said rather than to take out one example of one person. Mr. Tieger was talking about the army and the police sweeping through those areas, rounding up many, during which hundreds of non-Serbs were killed. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I heard that there was mopping up done by the police and the army, but I told you the reason why it was done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And did you also hear that large numbers of non-Serbs were killed during those operations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sir, you must have known from at least your conversation with this man, Mr. Zec, that these operations were brutal and bloody and that the non-Serbs of Prijedor were suffering grievously from those operations; correct?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO MANDIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't talk to him about these operations. You understand? I said: How come you are here? He said: I waited out the mopping-up operation. Could you just help me get to the station. And that man now lives in Vienna. We didn't really happen to talk about what was going on on the ground. I didn't discuss those details with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And you claim not to be aware that these areas were cleansed of their inhabitants, of their non-Serb population during that time? This is right in your municipality.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO MANDIC
utterances.text: I knew that it was cleansed, mopped up. I don't know if people were killed and how many. I couldn't know what was happening on the ground, in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: But UNPROFOR in Belgrade informed by Mr. Izetbegovic in Sarajevo knew about the devastation to non-Serbs in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO MANDIC
utterances.text: Well, they must have been in the field or got information from those who were in the field. I didn't go there. I don't know. You know, we didn't all meet with UNPROFOR and the head people. The president met with them and we were busy doing different work.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I tender 11302, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 11302 receives number P6954.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Mandic, in paragraph 35 of your statement you assert that the law enforcement organs in the Prijedor municipality conducted investigations against both known and unknown perpetrators and filed misdemeanour and criminal reports against them all. In fact, Mr. Mandic, you don't know if the police or the courts prosecuted the perpetrators of any crimes against non-Serbs during the war; correct? And that was something you admitted in the Karadzic case.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO MANDIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Mandic, if you admitted that in the Karadzic case - the Chamber has not looked at it - why does it then still appear in your statement which was given after the Karadzic case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's just left over from the earlier statement. The statement was not revised, that's why these things happen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you then tell us what happened during the taking of that statement. You say it was not revised. I take it that you were interviewed and that the statement was made and that you told the interviewers what you knew and that you would leave out what had turned out not to be reliable during your Karadzic testimony. Or did that not happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Some passages remained that simply -- they were not harmonised with the evidence given in the Karadzic case, the President Karadzic case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do we have to understand that part of your statement is just a left over of an interview that took place before your Karadzic testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Something like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you nevertheless attested at the beginning of your testimony that it was all accurate and truthful.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not a lawyer and simply such things -- I don't know how to explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, well, let me tell you clearly that we are at a point where I have to warn you if you say: I didn't think about my attestation, whether what is found in my statement is truthful or not, then perhaps you should consider to withdraw that because let's not forget that if you say it's truthful and if it now turns out that it's just a left over which you, not being a lawyer, stayed although you had been examined on the matter in Karadzic, that comes close to giving false testimony. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I'm aware of that, but it was not my intention to lie. I have no reason to lie, to perjure myself. I wouldn't have come here for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have warned you now four or five times only today. Is that clear to you? If you say: My attestation is not reliable, then please tell us at this moment. And if you say: I want to think about it, then you'll be given an opportunity.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I please think about it or could I perhaps consult lawyers? I really don't understand, believe me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, you're not allowed to consult a lawyer at this moment, at least not the lawyers of Mr. Mladic. If you say that the attestation you gave earlier today may not be reliable, then please tell us; and if you say: I want to think about it, then you'll have an opportunity to do that during the next break. At the same time, I have to warn you, if you're not telling us the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth, that you expose yourself to being prosecuted for false testimony and that you are at risk to be punished with a term of imprisonment of seven years. I have to warn you. Listen carefully to the next question of Mr. Tieger. You have an opportunity to think about your own statement during the break. And please be aware that every single word you're telling us should be the truth, not only the truth, but the whole truth and nothing but truth. Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I just have one more matter, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Mandic, you provided evidence in your statement about the fighting in Prijedor town on the 30th of May, 1992, following the attack on Prijedor town and its resolution, that is, the fact that it was dealt with relatively quickly by the Serbian police and military authorities. The neighbourhood known as Stari Grad was essentially destroyed by the VRS; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO MANDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And in fact after that happened, the Crisis Staff issued a number of decisions completing the demolition of Stari Grad; right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO MANDIC
utterances.text: I don't understand, which decisions?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: To demolish the structure -- to finally completely level the structures that had been demolished or destroyed by the VRS attack.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO MANDIC
utterances.text: That has to do with the lists of property, the inventory. Could you please explain that to me. A commission was set up to make a list of property that had been demolished during the war operations. Is that that?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, no, I was simply talking about the physical -- the demolition of the remaining ruins but it's not important. My main focus was on the aftermath of the attack itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And that in fact was my last subject, Mr. President, and concludes the examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tieger. I think it would be best to take the break a bit earlier than we would usually do so as to give the witness an opportunity to think about his statement. Witness, we'll take an early break. I advised you to think about whether your attestation given at the beginning of your testimony was a valid attestation. If you have any doubt, please tell us after the break. You may now follow the usher and we would like to see you back in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we take the break, Mr. Lukic, have you read the testimony of this witness in the Karadzic case?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I did, Your Honour, only when this witness came here to The Hague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, nevertheless you present as evidence his statement without any further question -- questions in which - and I just limit myself to the line raised by Mr. Tieger - paragraph 35: "The law enforcement organs, the prosecutor's office of Prijedor municipality conducted investigations against both known and unknown perpetrators and filed misdemeanour and criminal reports against them all." We do understand that the witness did not deny what was put to him by Mr. Tieger, and again we haven't read that so we have no opinion about that, but at least the witness did not deny that he had withdrawn from that in his Karadzic testimony. Is --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What he explained is that he has general knowledge, that he has some, that's more hearsay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He never claimed that he conducted investigations --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So--

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- then the questions that you should have put to this witness if you would not have even withdrawn his statement, you should have asked the witness: The last line of paragraph 35, is that your personal knowledge or is it what you heard or et cetera? I mean, it comes -- much of what the witness is supposed to have said here turns out to be what he may have heard or not heard, a lot of things he said facing the documents he had to step back from what he said. And the witness just presents those as facts, and if he doesn't know and again I would like -- as a matter of fact, I'd like to see the portion in the Karadzic statement where he steps back from it, whether he said: Well, I do know but not all the details. Or did he say: Well, actually, it's only what I heard but I have no personal knowledge? Would you agree that we look at that portion which apparently Mr. Tieger had on his mind so that we know what situation we are facing as a Chamber at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have no problems with that, but I think that everything is line with his -- today's answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that doesn't make it -- of course I'm discussing this because of your own responsibility, not only for the witness but also for you presenting this statement without any further questions, without any further comments. Therefore, Mr. Tieger, is there any way we could read on our screens the relevant portion of the Karadzic statement -- testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It's 65 ter 31659 at page 34.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Lukic, if there's any other portion that you consider to be relevant in this context, of course we'd look at that as well. Perhaps we just read it from our screens. This Chamber can read, the Judges of this Chamber. Perhaps could we go back one page or is that because it seems that it -- in the introduction is found in the previous page or is it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, you could direct us to the relevant portion on the page?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sure. The question was: "I'm asking you about the bodies you belong to, the Crisis Staff and the executive" -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you're reading --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] that side of the -- there's a discussion about this aspect, and I don't want to go back any farther than necessary. The alleged prosecution and so on, it's somewhat detailed. But then we begin by saying: "So in your statement" -- this is at the bottom of page 33. "So in your statement when you said police organs in the prosecutor's office of the Prijedor municipality undertook various investigations and filed misdemeanours and criminal reports against perpetrators, what exactly is that based on if you can only name one murder incident and you don't even know if the perpetrator was prosecuted? "A. Well, I assumed that everybody did what they were supposed to do, that courts and the prosecutor's office did what they were supposed to and the police did the same. One couldn't just turn a blind eye on events that happened because they did happen, and I suppose that they documented those things and that they caught the perpetrators. There were talks about various people who had done things. I didn't go to the police or to the court to ask whether they followed through or not and who the perps were."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, that sounds very much as just an assumption, that everyone did what they were supposed to do rather than global knowledge of what happened. It's just assumptions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour. He started that sentence, only in English you have two sentences, in B/C/S it's one. He started that sentence: "It is common knowledge ..." And then also --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- in that sentence you have "the prosecution" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then if you know that there's a difference, why didn't you check that? Why does the witness say that this was just left overs and that -- I mean, it's not the first time that this Chamber raises issues, and we know that we blamed for being partial in this respect, we've seen that before. But, Mr. Lukic, if the B/C/S says something different, then we'd like to have that verified --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- during the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's one sentence, that's what changes, that this "general knowledge" is -- actually applies to the second sentence in English --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- as well, the law, that law enforcement organs --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What I see is: "It is common knowledge that individual and all manner of killings took place, that is common knowledge." Now, the next sentence --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Which is the same sentence in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we'll need to --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was comma instead of full stop in B/C/S. But probably it's easier to translate in English with breaking here. I don't even blame the translators, but really in B/C/S it's one sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. What we'll try to find out, whether CLSS during the break would be in a position to explain to the Chamber whether the phrase in paragraph 35 starting with "it is common knowledge," whether linguistically the "common knowledge" would also extend to what follows after "the law enforcement organs, the prosecutor's office of Prijedor conducted investigations against both known and unknown perpetrators and filed misdemeanour and criminal reports against them all." Because the English translation does not suggest that the common law -- the common knowledge phrase extends to that part. If that is debatable, if that's not perhaps what after verification turns out to be the case, then the Chamber would like to know that. Madam Registrar, I know that we are asking the impossible from CLSS and we have done that already so many times, but if this portion of the transcript, together with paragraph 35 of the witness's statement could be given to CLSS and if we -- if only we could have a provisional opinion about the question we have put, then the Chamber would appreciate to know that before we resume and we intend to resume at quarter past 1.00 and we'll take a break until then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Welcome back, Mr. Mandic. I asked you to think about the attestation you've given --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- at the beginning of your testimony, and I'll go through the questions again that were put by Mr. Lukic. After you had made a correction to your statement, you changed the date from 30th of May to 30th of April, Mr. Lukic asked you whether the statement, after this correction, whether the facts stated in this statement, whether they are accurate as you told them to the Defence team of General Mladic. Could you -- you then answered "yes." Is your answer still "yes," that this is what you told the Defence team?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, the next question was whether the content of the statement was accurate and truthful.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My answer was yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And it still is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now we've established that a part is not adequate in relation to the time-period when communications were down between Prijedor and the Krajina, or rather, and Pale. That was established -- actually, maybe it was an oversight on my part during the defence of Mr. Karadzic. This was a shorter period of time, not several months.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, there have been other instances such as whether the take-over was triggered by the telegram or whether there have been other events which happened and before and that preparations were made already, that in that respect I think you also corrected your statement, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I added that because that is how I understood the question, what initiated the take-over. And then as the questions went on then we got to what was happening before that telegram on the 29th of April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There are other matters as well where you apparently seem to have no personal knowledge where you claimed facts to be as you described them, although not knowing personally about them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that I heard that not that I saw it. Do you understand that? I live in that town, I ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You often said things happened where, as we understand now, you wanted to say "I heard that it happened," which is not the same.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, yes, exactly. I mean, I tend to equate that and then it's my jargon and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do I then have to understand that whatever you present as facts, that we should seriously consider that they may not be facts but that it's just what you heard were the facts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, no. I mean, I think it's not really that much. I mean, we documented things and confirmed things, things that happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the last question that was put to you was whether you'd -- if the same questions would be put to you today, whether you'd answer the same. And I took it and from your answer I also took it that you understood it to be that in substance it would be the same answers to those questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that still stands, as far as you're concerned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but maybe my formulation is not as expected from me, I mean simply I'm not very skilful at this kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I have, before I give an opportunity to Mr. Lukic to re-examine you, I have one other question. You were asked quite some questions by Mr. Tieger about massacres, people being killed, et cetera. Now, some of these events you stated that you had heard about it and so to that extent you knew about them, but they do not appear in your statement. Do you have an explanation as to why you give quite some details about all kind of things which now turn out to be hearsay rather than personal knowledge, whereas you didn't say anything about hearsay on such killings and massacres. Do you have an explanation as why you presented in hearsay what we find in your statement and that you did not present as hearsay what Mr. Tieger asked you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, quite simply, knowing that such and such a thing happened, that I heard about it, that's what shows that that kind of thing did happen, I mean I didn't state -- I don't know whether it's necessary to state that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would say that the killings were known anyhow, you don't have to state that? Or I do not fully understand perhaps what you are --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, yes, along those lines, yes, in that sense, yes, that it's generally known and that quite simply I assume that the Prosecution and the Court know that and I don't have to describe it additionally, and then there's also the public security station, the court, the prosecutor's office in Prijedor -- I mean, if they all did their job I assume that everybody should do their job, at least that's the way I've been taught.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you said all the nasty things that may have happened, you didn't include those in your statement, nasty things against non-Serbs, you didn't include them in your statement because they were commonly known and therefore there was no need to address them; is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what to say to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just answer the question, whether that's how we have to understand your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it's commonly known that it happened and I gave that statement, I said that this kind of thing happened and everything that happened is also there at the public security station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now you say this is what you stated, but as a matter of fact you did not state that it was common knowledge that non-Serbs were killed in Keraterm or that during operations, cleansing operations, a large number of non-Serbs were killed. You expressed yourself mainly on Serbs being attacked and Serbs being killed and not on non-Serbs being attacked and non-Serbs being killed, and I'm asking you what explains that. You spent quite a few words on killings and attacks against Serbs and that you apparently did not spend words on killings and massacres of non-Serbs. And I'm asking you whether what explains that you focused on one and did not say anything about the other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I cannot explain. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have no explanation for that. Then --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you allow me. Maybe, I thought at that moment that the Tribunal had information about what happened to non-Serbs but that it did not have information about what happened to Serbs. Perhaps that was my thinking. I mean, now that I'm so worked up I cannot really say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you there. Who gave you that impression?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, perhaps my very own personal impression. It's not that somebody else gave me this impression.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I leave it to that. Mr. Lukic, I will read what seems to be the provisional view of CLSS. It reads: "The B/C/S version consists of two co-ordinated sentences. 'Common knowledge' does not extend to the second part of the sentence. The English translation could also read: "'It is common knowledge that'" and then what follows and "'the law enforcement organs' ... et cetera." This is the provisional information we received from CLSS and of course it was done very quickly. Mr. Lukic, if you have any questions in re-examination, you may put them to the witness now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I can comment on this translation, I have to say that with full respect I do not agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. You do not agree. That's fine. Then we can argue that later on, but that is, and I said, provisional opinion given by CLSS and whether there's any room for further argument on the matter we'll learn that and you can make submissions at a later stage on that but we're not going to do that now. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Before I continue questioning this witness, I would just express our position regarding hearsay evidence in this court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not in the presence of the witness. You may do so -- we'll give you an opportunity to do that, but we would first like to see whether we can conclude the testimony of this witness. And if you say you need a lot of time, please be aware that the Chamber is not convinced that part of the problems are not due to the way in which you had taken the statement and how it was presented. So therefore, use your time as efficiently as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If we can see P6948 now, we'll start with that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mandic, first of all, good afternoon again.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO MANDIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this first paragraph as well as paragraph 3, number 1, namely that in leading positions, in management positions, what positions were meant exactly, do you know?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO MANDIC
utterances.text: This is a very broad concept. I think it means public security, the army, and some other agencies and authorities where reliable people were needed, people loyal to the authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was the intention to include butchers, tradesmen?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO MANDIC
utterances.text: No, only people who made important decisions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: How do you understand, Mr. Witness, the phrase that says: "All posts of importance for the functioning of economic entities," what would that include?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That would be the electrical distribution company, that means power transmission, also telecom, telephone providers, some means of communication such as railways.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are we to understand you to be saying that butchers and tradesmen are not part of economic entities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, may I remind you that the focus was on whether the test was ethnicity or anything else and that's -- that's the most important element rather than to spend a lot of time on defining on whether position A would just fall within or just fall outside the scope of what is mentioned here. The document is clear in this respect, that it is not any post, not just everything, it should have a certain importance. But the focus, if I understand the questions of Mr. Tieger well, is about whether ethnicity was, at least in the beginning of paragraph 1 the item, and that loyalty would be an item for those who were of Serb ethnicity. That is the issue which is central to the questions put by Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's why I directed the attention of this witness to paragraph 3 of the same. So where it says: "Likewise, these posts may not be held by these employees of Serbian ethnicity who have not confirmed in the plebiscite or have not yet accepted that the only representative of the Serbian people is a Serbian Democratic Party."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, now, it's -- I mean --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just want to clarify which positions this addresses, so no Muslims, no Croats, no Serbs according to this document on these positions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- or Serbs who are not loyal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the witness has any factual knowledge about it and otherwise the interpretation of this document is for the parties and for the Bench to further consider. And it's perfectly clear that the decision excludes in general terms non-Serbs and further excludes Serbs to the extent they are not loyal. That seems prima facie what the document tells. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mandic, did parties nominate their candidates for these positions?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO MANDIC
utterances.text: I don't understand what you mean, what parties? The SDS was the only party.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before the take-over.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO MANDIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was a division of power and each party nominated its members for different positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the time when this decision was made, power had been taken over and SDS was in power; correct?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO MANDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In July 1992 -- [In English] That was part of my previous question, so I got an answer "yes." I will move now to the next topic regarding Crisis Staffs. [Interpretation] My learned friend Mr. Tieger put it to you earlier today that the Crisis Staff existed before the take-over. First I'd like to ask you: To the best of your knowledge was there one Crisis Staff in Prijedor or several?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO MANDIC
utterances.text: In which period? Because we've now established --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's say in the entire year of 1992, was one Crisis Staff organised in Prijedor or more than one?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO MANDIC
utterances.text: According to some information I have, at the public security station there was a separate Crisis Staff, apart from the Crisis Staff of the municipality of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know if the SDS had their own Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO MANDIC
utterances.text: We've just established here that some sort of Crisis Staff existed, and now we see, in various sessions which I did not attend, it existed physically. So obviously there was an SDS Crisis Staff. It was present on the ground.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you know that it was present on the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I meant those decisions of the Municipal Board of the SDS, that's what I was alluding to, the Crisis Staff. If they were calling themselves "Crisis Staff," then they should have been present or it was written erroneously, not "local commune" but "Crisis Staff."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So you attended meetings from what I understood from your testimony in which tasks and functioning of a Crisis Staff was discussed before the 30th of April?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: These are the facts you know. Do you know anything more about those Crisis Staffs, who were members of it, where they met, what they did? Do you know anything about it? Not what you ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think the chairman of the Crisis Staff was Simo Miskovic from the Municipal Board of the SDS. Another member was also a deputy. There may even be a list of people who were members of the Crisis Staff ex officio. If we could get that document shown me by the Prosecutor earlier, we could see the names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say: I think the chairman of the Crisis Staff was Simo Miskovic. Why do you think that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, that's how I express myself. I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but what do you know? Did he tell you? Is it on the basis of the meetings that you learned that he was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, based on the meetings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed -- Mr. Lukic, I only want facts and the Chamber wants facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll see the facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not thoughts, not opinions. Facts. So the witness heard during the meetings that Simo Miskovic was the chairman of the Crisis Staff. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we see P3733, please. I apologise, it's P3773. That's a document we received later, so I would just kindly ask to see the bottom of the page. We need the next page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Under number 2 you see at the bottom of the page in B/C/S it says: "Commander of the Crisis Staff shall be the president of the Municipal Board of the SDS of Prijedor." This document was shown to you earlier by the Prosecution. You told us today that you'd heard this before, but did you see this document before today, before the Prosecution showed it to you?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO MANDIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Who was the president of the Municipal Board of the SDS of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO MANDIC
utterances.text: Simo Miskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we've cleared that up, let us clear up when the Crisis Staff of which you were a member was established. Let me show you a document that we tendered as an associated exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P4086.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can I ask whether there's any dispute about a Crisis Staff in which the witness was appointed being established at a later point in time? Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, I'm at something of a disadvantage because I'm not conversant with the testimony of all witnesses who preceded this witness. I presume we may be discussing the distinction between a Crisis Staff that pre-existed the conflict and Crisis Staff that existed in the aftermath of the Djeric instructions which this Court received, but I'm not sure about the nuances in which that distinction has been presented so I would be a little reluctant to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So there may be some dispute about that. Mr. Lukic, the focus was on how reliable the testimony of the witness was, which was talking about a Crisis Staff established after the 30th of April, where the witness, as he testified now, was aware of the existence of a Crisis Staff, whether the same or not exactly the same, prior to that. And I think that the Prosecution introduced that evidence in order to -- for the Chamber to assess the reliability and the credibility of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger seems to -- seems to confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, in paragraph 6 of his statement this gentleman is explicitly addressing a particular Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and he --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And he says --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- doesn't say anything about the other Crisis Staff that he was apparently aware of that existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My colleague Tieger tried to say that this paragraph 6 is not truthful and I'm telling you it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I think as a matter of fact that it has been established now that it's at least not the whole of the truth. Let's leave it to that for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, no, this paragraph is exactly truthful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And I'll tell you why.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The whole truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It says: "The Council for National Defence" [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, one second.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "The Council for National Defence..." --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, one second.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- "... decided" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Mr. Lukic, you may ask questions and then elicit the matter you want to further --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Mr. Mandic, in 6 you say: "After the peaceful take-over of power in Prijedor on the 30th of April, 1992, the Council for National Defence adopted a decision to set up a Crisis Staff in order to more easily overcome the newly arisen complex political and security situation in the municipality of Prijedor." The Council for National Defence --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us look at the period before, P2871, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mandic, we are looking at the record from the 4th Session of the Council for National Defence of the Prijedor municipality dated 15 May, 1992. Under agenda item 1, it says: "Decision on the organisation and functioning of the Crisis Staff." Down below under conclusions number 1 on the same page, it says: "The draft decision on the organisation and functioning of the Crisis Staff is hereby accepted with the proviso that a representative of the garrison in Prijedor be added to the proposed list of members of the Crisis Staff." Before this date and before this draft, did there exist a Crisis Staff of which you were a member?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO MANDIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us look at P4086. It's another document tendered by the Prosecution today as associated to your testimony. We read here: "Pursuant to Article 110 of the Constitution of the Serbian Republic in Article 4 of the decision of the organisation and work of Prijedor municipal Crisis Staff, the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor at its session held on 20th May 1992 adopted the following decision on appointments to the Prijedor municipal Crisis Staff ..." Were you a member of that Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO MANDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now it says for the president, vice-president, and members of the Crisis Staff, the following people are appointed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We see the president and vice-president under numbers 1 and 2 and who's the man under number 5?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO MANDIC
utterances.text: My humble self.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need page 2 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We see this was signed by the president of the Municipal Assembly and the date is 20 May 1992. Do you have direct knowledge that the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor decided to set up the Crisis Staff for the municipality of Prijedor on 20th May 1992?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO MANDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We've seen in a previous document which was a record from a session of the Council for National Defence dated 15 May 1992 that there was a proposal for a member of the garrison to be also included in the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see in e-court 65 ter 31674.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As you can see, Mr. Mandic, we have before us an issue of the Official Gazette of the municipality of Prijedor of 25 June 1992, and we see that it promulgates the decision on the organisation and work of the Prijedor municipal Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will need paragraph 4 -- Article 4 in fact. Next page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It says in this Article 4 of the decision published in the Official Gazette that: "The Crisis Staff of Prijedor municipality consists of a president, a vice-president, and nine members. "The president of the Municipal Assembly shall serve ex officio as the president of the Crisis Staff and the vice-president of the Municipal Assembly as the vice-president of the Crisis Staff." And then follow the names of the members, indicating each of their positions. Where do you see yourself in this list, could you please read till the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need to move to the next page in English --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I'm again asking Mr. Tieger, this Crisis Staff, the establishment of this after the take-over, is that in dispute, irrespective of whether there was another Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, Mr. President, it's not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So then we don't have -- that's accepted by -- there's no dispute about this Crisis Staff being established. Again, Mr. Lukic, the issue was whether the witness had given the whole of the truth, and if you say A established a Crisis Staff, then there are a few options. And I don't think Mr. Tieger in this respect in view of his questions, although he expressed himself not very accurately in this respect by saying this is not true, I think what Mr. Tieger intended to establish is that there was at least a Crisis Staff prior to that date which is relevant in this context and that by the line -- the statement by the witness that this may have given an impression which does not reflect the whole of the situation. I think that's the issue and there's no further dispute about this Crisis Staff being established under those circumstances at a later stage. And we do know, and you have, I think, and there seems to be no dispute about that, that that other Crisis Staff was established not exactly by the secretary of National Defence but still a Crisis Staff functioning in the Prijedor context. That seems to be the issue. If there's any further question to be asked about that, please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, in regard of this paragraph it's not only mentioned it was double safe-guard. It says first "Council for National Defence decided," and the first safe-guard is: "Following a peaceful take-over of power in Prijedor on 30th of April, 1992." So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's exactly where the dispute is, whether this presents a truthful picture by not saying anything about the other Crisis Staff and exclusively dealing with this Crisis Staff. That's exactly the issue. I don't think that the witness can help us out very much. I'm not --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have no problem with that if you are going to apply the same standard to Prosecutor witnesses. I have no problem with that. But we have to go back to every single witness of the Prosecution and see what they did mention in their statements and what we elicited from their cross-examination. If that's the same standard, I'm ready to sacrifice this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If a witness presents a picture by leaving out other elements which are relevant and give a distorted picture of the events, I think that this Chamber has always been very alert to establish that, and certainly in cross-examination the Defence has done a good job in many respects.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: With all due respect, we do not agree with your --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not -- I do not --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- that it's a distorted truth. It's not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am not seeking your agreement. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Still we need to conclude with this document because it's not in evidence and we think it's crucial because it rebuts the evidence of several Prosecution witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You can tender it and then we'll hear from Mr. Tieger whether there's any objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Because in this document we can see the members --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- if you want to tender it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do want to tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, document with number 31674 receives number D827.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Still I'll need some clarification from the witness since he's the only witness from the Crisis Staff for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mandic, could you please tell us where you recognise yourself in Article 4 because there is no reference to any names here. I'm sorry, I've just been told that the question has not been interpreted. Where do you recognise yourself in paragraph 4? Because there are no names that have been referred to.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO MANDIC
utterances.text: The second line of the second paragraph: "The commander of the municipal staff of civilian defence ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could we see the first page -- the earlier page of --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- or the first part of paragraph 4 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It reads commander of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah, it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- municipal people's defence staff. That is what --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Should be civilian defence, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's a translation issue. But that's where the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- finds that he was a member -- appointed member of that Crisis Staff. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mandic, among these posts and later in the work of the Crisis Staff, was there anyone from the garrison or from the army there? Do you see this amongst these positions that are referred to?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO MANDIC
utterances.text: If you are addressing me, I did not understand the question or maybe I didn't hear it. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Among these office holders, are there any members of the Army of Republika Srpska here and were any members of the Army of Republika Srpska members of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO MANDIC
utterances.text: No. No one from the Army of Republika Srpska is on the list of members of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I see it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm looking at the clock. How much time would you still need?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm trying to calculate now. Probably not more than 15, 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Tomorrow you have 15 minutes. We'll -- Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Just very quickly, Mr. President. I think the Court went a long way to clarifying the issue of the Crisis Staffs. I just wanted to respond more explicitly to something the Court asked about the reasons for introducing evidence related to that. You focused on credibility assessment and of course that's in part true but it was also obviously so that the Court would have a more full and proper evidential basis to asses the breach take-over circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The existence of a Crisis Staff there and the discussions on the A and B Variants. That's understood. Mr. Mandic, we'll not finish today. We'd like to see you back tomorrow morning. It will be a short session. Mr. Tieger, could you already give an estimate as matters stand now as to how much time you would need?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: None.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mandic, we would like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30 in this same courtroom, and I have to instruct you that you should not speak with anyone about your testimony, whether it is testimony already given or still to be given tomorrow. So no communication with whomever. If that is clear to you, you may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is clear to me, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day and we'll resume tomorrow, Thursday, the 27th of November, 9.30 in the morning in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 27th day of November, 2014, at 9.30 a.m. 24 25
